final.paragraph:
This is an automated hazard-exposure briefing produced by Riprap from live and precomputed data sources. It is informational only and not a substitute for a professional risk assessment.

**Answer.**
From the sources consulted: The National Weather Service forecasts a peak water level of 6.0 ft above MLLW at The Battery, the nearest forecast gauge (1 km away), on 2026-10-04 19:00 UTC (forecast issued 2026-10-02 07:58 UTC), below the gauge's minor flood stage of 7.0 ft [nws_water_forecast]. Latest reading at The Battery, NY: 5.03 ft above MLLW (+0.17 ft vs predicted tide), observed 2026-10-02 15:30 UTC [noaa_tides]. Experimental forecast: the water at The Battery may run up to 0.16 m (0.5 ft) above NOAA's predicted tide in the next 96 hours, counted from 2026-10-02 15:00 UTC, most around 2026-10-05 16:00 UTC; added to the predicted tide, the highest total would be 5.7 ft above MLLW on 2026-10-02 17:00 UTC, below the gauge's minor flood stage of 7.0 ft [ttm_battery_surge]. Limits: it reads only the last 1,024 hours of the Battery gauge, with no wind or pressure input, so it cannot see a storm that has not yet reached the gauge; on 635 past 96-hour windows (2025-01-01 to 2026-09-27) its mean error was 11.5 cm, against 13.3 cm for assuming the last day's mean continues, and it foresaw 1 of the 23 windows in which the water reached the minor flood stage [ttm_battery_surge]. Rely on the National Weather Service (weather.gov/okx) and Notify NYC; NOAA's ETSS and the Stevens Flood Advisory System model surge from the weather [ttm_battery_surge].

**Out of scope.** This briefing does not assess title, structural condition, or compliance with specific zoning rules. Where a probe was offline at run time, the relevant section omits that signal.

Checks run: citations and numbers on every claim; lead rules on the answer, which is the cited text word for word.
